label: Давать
description: A 10-sentence conjugation card for давать (to give).

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: First-person singular present. 'Даю' comes from the special stem да-, dropping -ва- in the present, plus the ending -ю. 'Давать совет' means to give advice; 'тебе' is the dative recipient.
Strategic focus: Second-person singular present. 'Даёшь' uses the stressed -ёшь ending on the present stem да-. 'Мне' is the dative recipient and 'силы' the accusative object.
Strategic focus: Third-person singular present. 'Даёт' is the он-form with stressed -ёт. The verb takes a dative recipient 'нам' and an accusative object 'задание'.
Strategic focus: First-person plural present. 'Даём' is the мы-form ending in -ём. 'Детям' is the dative recipient and 'свободы' the genitive after 'много'.
Strategic focus: Third-person plural present. 'Дают' closes the present set with the -ют ending on the stem да-. 'Деньги' is the accusative object of the donation.
Strategic focus: Masculine past tense. 'Давал' is the masculine singular past of imperfective давать, keeping the full -ва- stem. The perfective partner дать would stress a single completed act.
Strategic focus: Feminine past tense. 'Давала' adds the feminine -а ending. 'Часто' underlines the repeated nature, exactly what the imperfective expresses.
Strategic focus: Plural past tense. 'Давали' is the plural past ending in -и. 'Детям' stays dative and 'свободу' is the accusative object.
Strategic focus: Perfective future, first-person. 'Дам' is the irregular perfective дать with future meaning, signalling a single completed act. 'Завтра' marks the time and 'тебе' the recipient.

missions.phrase: Давай мне руку и не бойся!
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Singular imperative. 'Давай' is the informal command of давать, built on the present stem да-. Beyond literally giving, 'давай' also serves as the everyday Russian let's-go particle.
